newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, seen up if U.S. news good.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, seen up if U.S. news good.

text.p: Polish shares extended Thursday's slight gain and analysts said the surprisingly strong buying after price-fixing and at continuous trade signalled moderate rises next.
They said the potential rises could be slowed if Friday's U.S. jobless data showed high employment and caused Dow falls due to expected U.S. interest rate rises.
"If today's information is good and would delay the possibility of an interest rate rise...I think we could have rises next week," said Kamil Kalemba, a trader at ING Barings in Warsaw.
Analysts said the prices of some stocks had become attractive after the market's fall from its three-year high at 18,339.4 points on February 18.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.1 percent to 15,670.2 points and turnover fell 29.6 percent to 139.1 million zlotys on all three markets.

Analysts said Kredyt Bank, whose 3.7-percent rise made it the main market's fourth top gainer, should continue to benefit from Friday's news it had won a tender to buy Polish Investment Bank (PBI) and Prosper Bank.
Analysts said debt-ridden builder Espebepe SA, down 9.6 percent and 19 percent on the week, was falling as speculators continued to play on the firm's unclear fate.
The firm, which has 75 million zlotys in debt and a creditors' meeting due on April 14, surged 41.9 percent last week after the previous week's steep fall.
Analysts said Zasada's 9.6-percent fall in light trade was a reaction to recent rises.
